findings.reason: §9's own deliverable and done-when add the test that composes the loader into a brief, so correcting "called by tests" to "called by nothing" changes no work the section prescribes.
findings.text: §9 states "`load_review_prompt` … is called by tests and by no production path, and the same is true of `load_claims_review_prompt`, added by §8": `load_claims_review_prompt` (`reckon/crew/review.py:437`) has no caller anywhere in the tree — `grep -rn load_claims_review_prompt` returns only its definition — so §9 overstates how far §8 exercised its loader, and an implementer reusing it can assume a validated path that does not exist

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every citation resolves in the tree: `recovery_review_subject.py:503` blanks the brief when a plan is set, `:496-502` is the plan-authority invariant, `recovery_review_subject.py:598-601` is the `--brief` XOR `--plan`/`--section` pair §9 cites as 597-601, `recovery_classification.py:550` calls `_review_dispatch_action`, and the cited run prompt exists at 141 lines with the dimensions named only in its done-when.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — `tests/test_a_review_receives_its_rubric.py` names a falsifiable assertion set (SCORE block and every dimension name in the implement run's brief, CLAIM grammar in the investigate run's brief, --plan/--section beside --brief for a plan-naming run) with a declared negative control that fails the first assertion when the brief is composed from the reviewed run's brief alone.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §9 writes no scratch evidence; its only on-disk deliverable is a test under `tests/`, and its negative-control log is delivered on the run's `test_logs`/manifest, so no gate log lands in a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §9's new names are mechanism terms (`SCORE`/`CLAIM` grammar, `_review_dispatch_fields`/`_tokens`/`_action`); no plan labels or ticket numbers reach code, and the §-references live only in the plan's own prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §9's evidence sentence claims `load_claims_review_prompt` is "called by tests and by no production path", but the loader is called by nothing at all, not even a test.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9 carries one deliverable: a run review's composed brief carries its rubric, read from one place by both the reflex dispatch and the obligation's next command.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §9's only needed dependency is §8's claims loader, which §8 landed at 430105036 and §9 states it runs on; no depends-on/informs/gates edge points at the wrong node.
